;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**At least ten people have been killed in a [[shootout]] between jailed [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] militants and security officers at a prison in [[Mogadishu]], [[Somalia]]. An investigation is under way into how the militants obtained weapons, with some reports suggested that an inmate disarmed a warden and then a group of them raided the armoury. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53733967 (BBC News)]
*[[Afghan peace process]]
**[[Taliban]] spokesman Suhail Shaheen warns that attacks on newly freed prisoners will drive them back to the battlefield despite orders from their leaders. The [[government of Afghanistan|government]] denies attacking, or re-arresting them without cause. [https://www.thehour.com/news/article/Taliban-warn-against-attacks-on-freed-prisoners-15474830.php (''The Hour'')]
*[[Gaza–Israel clashes in 2020]]
**[[Israel]] launches multiple airstrikes in the [[Gaza Strip]] after [[Palestinian airborne arson attacks|incendiary balloons launch from Gaza into Israel]]. [https://www.haaretz.com/hblocked?returnTo=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.haaretz.com%2Fisrael-news%2F.premium-israel-strikes-hamas-targets-in-gaza-over-incendiary-balloons-1.9065692 (''Haaretz'')]
*Benoît Maria, a [[French people|French]] [[Human rights defender|human rights activist]] who helped [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas#Guatemala|indigenous people]] in [[Guatemala]], is shot dead while driving near [[San Antonio Ilotenango]] in [[Quiché Department|Quiché]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53735508 (BBC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 recession]]
**[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
***The [[Office for National Statistics]] reports the worst quarterly job losses in the [[United Kingdom]] since the [[Great Recession|financial crisis]] in 2009. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-53733440 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
***[[Singapore]] enters technical recession for the first time in a decade after [[Economy of Singapore|its economy]] contracts by 13.2% in the second quarter, which translates to a record 42.9% plunge in its annualised [[GDP]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/business/economy/singapore-lowers-2020-gdp-forecast-to-between-5-and-7-as-economy-plunges-worse-than (''The Straits Times'')]
*[[Facebook]] introduces new regulations blocking [[United States|American]] publishers with political ties from running ads masquerading as news articles in its [[News Feed|news section]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-facebook-elections/facebook-places-curbs-on-ads-by-u-s-news-publishers-with-political-ties-idUSKCN2571Y0 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] imposes a curfew on bars, restaurants, and cafes in several regions following an increase in COVID-19 cases. The curfew lasts from midnight until 7 a.m. local time. [https://www.itv.com/news/2020-08-11/greece-curfew-on-bars-and-restaurants-as-coronavirus-cases-rise (ITV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] announces the approval of a [[vaccine]] against COVID‑19, named [[Gam-COVID-Vac]], claiming it as a "world-first", amid continued concern and unanswered questions over its safety and effectiveness. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/08/11/europe/russia-coronavirus-vaccine-putin-intl/index.html (CNN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] records 1,148 cases, their highest since June 21. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-britain-cases/uk-records-1148-new-confirmed-covid-19-cases-idUSKCN2572D7 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] suspends its seasonal ban on the harvest, sale, and consumption of [[coral trout]] and [[grouper]] to fight economic hardships during the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/423211/fiji-suspends-ban-on-fish-to-ease-economic-woes (RNZ)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****[[New Zealand]] reports its first cases of community transmission in 102 days, four cases in a single family. [[Auckland]] will move to Alert Level 3 from August 12 at 12 noon until midnight on August 14. The rest of the country will move to Alert Level 2. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12355759 (''New Zealand Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bhutan]]
***[[Bhutan]] imposes a nationwide lockdown after a locally transmitted COVID-19 case was reported in Gelephu town and the female patient had come in close contact with many people in Paro, Thimphu and several other places. [https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/bhutan-govt-imposes-nationwide-lockdown-to-curb-coronavirus-spread-120081100437_1.html (''Business Standard'')]
**The total number of worldwide confirmed cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] surpasses 20 million. The United States remains the global leader of case numbers, accounting for more than 25 percent cumulative.  [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/08/10/health/20-million-coronavirus-cases-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Natick, Massachusetts|Natick]], [[Massachusetts]], issues town-wide water restrictions, limiting water use by Natick residents, in response to an ongoing [[drought]] affecting most parts of [[New England]]. [https://patch.com/massachusetts/natick/natick-water-ban-goes-effect-amid-drought-threat (Patch)]

;Law and crime
*[[Piracy in the Gulf of Guinea]]
**Three men are fined by a court in [[Port Harcourt]], [[Nigeria]], for hijacking the [[oil tanker]] MV ''Elobey VI'' off the coast of [[Equatorial Guinea]] and holding the crew hostage for [[United States dollar|US$]]200,000 in March. They are the first people to be convicted under Nigeria's new anti-piracy law. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nigeria-security-piracy/nigeria-convicts-first-pirates-under-new-maritime-law-idUSKCN2581EL?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Bangalore riots]]
**The violent clashes took place in eastern [[Bangalore]], [[Karnataka]], India. The violence cause the death of at least 3 people in police firing while injuring 60 police personnel during the clashes. [https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/bangalore/in-bengalurus-kaval-byrasandra-mlas-house-attacked-over-derogatory-post-by-relative-6550820/ (''The Indian Express'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**[[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[Marion County, Florida]], Sheriff Billy Woods forbids his employees and those visiting his offices from  wearing face masks in most circumstances. The [[Ocala, Florida|Ocala City Council]] passed an emergency ordinance last week requiring people to wear masks inside businesses.  Ocala’s mayor, Kent Guinn, vetoed the county rule on Monday. [https://www.ocala.com/news/20200811/marion-county-deputies-ordered-not-to-wear-masks (''The Ocala Star-Banner'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/08/12/us/fl-sheriff-billy-woods-bans-masks.html (''The New York Times'')] 
*[[2020 Belarusian presidential election]], [[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**[[Belarus]]ian opposition leader [[Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]] flees Belarus to her family in [[Lithuania]], according to [[government of Lithuania|Lithuanian]] [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Lithuania)|Foreign Minister]] [[Linas Antanas Linkevičius]]. Tsikhanouskaya had gone into hiding after the disputed election, which she accuses [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] of rigging. [https://reuters.com/article/uk-belarus-election/belarusian-opposition-leader-tikhanouskaya-safe-in-lithuania-after-clashes-idUKKCN2570SO (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Egyptian Senate election]]
**Citizens of [[Egypt]] head to the polls to elect 200 members of the newly created [[Senate (Egypt)|senate]]. The new [[upper house]] of the [[Parliament of Egypt|parliament]] will be an advisory body only and is expected to be dominated by supporters of [[President of Egypt|president]] [[Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-egypt-election-senate/egyptians-vote-for-newly-created-senate-idUSKCN2570WA (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Malian protests]]
**Anti-[[government of Mali|government]] protests resume in the [[Mali]]an capital of [[Bamako]], as thousands take to the street demanding the resignation of President [[Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta]] after talks between the government and the protesters stalled. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/08/anti-gov-protests-resume-mali-weeks-long-pause-200811163841598.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2020 Trinidad and Tobago general election]]
**Preliminary results see the ruling [[People’s National Movement]] winning a plurality of 22 seats in [[Trinidad and Tobago]]'s latest election. The [[United National Congress]] is assumed to come in second with 19 seats. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-trinidadtobago-election/trinidad-and-tobago-pm-claims-election-victory-for-ruling-party-idUSKCN2570E4 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 United States presidential election]], [[2020 Democratic Party vice presidential candidate selection]]
**Former [[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] [[Joe Biden]] chooses [[United States Senate|Senator]] [[Kamala Harris]] as his running mate, making her the presumptive 2020 Democratic vice presidential nominee. She is the first black woman and first Asian-American vice presidential nominee for a major party. [https://www.cnn.com/politics/live-news/2020-election-biden-vp-pick/index.html (CNN)]

;Science and technology
*[[France|French]] privacy watchdog group [[Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés|CNIL]] launches a preliminary investigation into [[TikTok]], as part of a [[European Union]]-wide taskforce monitoring the app's operations. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-france-tiktok-privacy/french-privacy-watchdog-opens-investigation-into-tiktok-idUSKCN25718J (Reuters)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**Two of the [[Power Five conferences|"Power Five" conferences]] of [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|Division I FBS]], the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] and [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] conferences, postpone their fall 2020 sports seasons due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The Pac-12 also announces that winter sports whose seasons were scheduled to begin in calendar year 2020, most notably basketball, will not start play until at least January 1, 2021. [https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/08/11/901081822/the-big-ten-postpones-football-other-fall-sports-over-coronavirus-concerns (NPR)] [https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/29640603/sources-pac-12-calls-fall-sports-eyes-spring (ESPN)]
